newsitem.title: UK: Low stocks keep the heat under world oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Low stocks keep the heat under world oil prices.

text.p: Low heating oil and diesel stocks in the United States and Europe kept the heat under world oil prices on Thursday, with Western consumers having barely dusted down their winter wardrobes.
Heating oil futures, at $231 a tonne in London and 71 cents a gallon in New York on Wednesday, are already running well above last winter's highs, set during one of the longest cold spells on record.
Benchmark Brent crude had traded 27 cents lower at $22.93 a barrel, but the drop was caused by profit taking and the fundamentals remain strong.
Worried refinery buyers, concerned that an early winter could eat into already depleted heating oil stocks, have scrambled for supplies this week.
Markets for heating oil in Rotterdam and New York Harbor both have seen premiums for prompt delivery rise quickly over the past couple of days.
Refiners and traders have bought heavily on futures markets to protect themselves against higher prices this winter. Speculators have bet on further price gains.
"It would be foolish to bet against this market going higher," said a dealer in London. "It would be like standing in front of a freight train."
U.S. industry and government data this week showed heating and diesel stocks running some 30 percent below 1995 levels in the key U.S. northeast region.

The recent sale of a number of cargoes from the United States to Europe has served as a significant brake on the replenishment of U.S. stocks, which are still 19 million barrels below year-ago levels for the country as a whole.
But stocks in Europe's biggest market, Germany, also are running well below normal.

Oil analysts said an oil company drive over the last two years to cut costs by operating "just-in-time" inventory practices would make markets vulnerable to further price spikes during periods of tight supply.

Markets are having to cope without several hundred thousand barrels a day of Iraqi crude supplies after a U.N. oil-for-food deal was put on hold indefinitely after Baghdad's military incursion into Kurdish safe havens earlier this month.
